structured_output.analysis: The best grid, iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e), measured KL=0.43614 at avg_bits 3.14795. The budget is 403/128 = 3.14844 bits, so there are only about 0.0005 bits per weight to spare. Every per-layer upgrade on the loss-concentration list costs about 1 bit per weight on a 3.1M-parameter MLP layer. Examples: 27.up gptq_int3→gptq_int4 (E04d8aa7bded→Efea8c18d2abc) and 14.down rht_gptq_int2→rht_gptq_int3 (E4c3f9b73e065→E90bd4b2f3645). Each would need an equal downgrade elsewhere. The retrieved records show no downgrade that costs less KL than these upgrades save, and the knapsack already balanced those single-layer trade-offs. The measured KL is about 0.038 above the prediction, which points to interaction or error accumulation that per-layer swaps cannot target. GPTQ options that do not change bit count are the best lever this round: act_order, damp and block_size cost no bits. This round tests those settings on all GPTQ-family methods and leaves the cell assignment unchanged.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: iso_3.15 measured KL=0.43614 (E514ab09c524e), and 178 of its cells use GPTQ-family methods. Setting act_order=true for every GPTQ-family method leaves the stored bits unchanged, so this stays within budget. The highest-loss layers have strongly heavy-tailed activations, for example activation kurtosis 1090.09 at 27.up (E24beed188b6a). Quantizing high-salience columns first should reduce the GPTQ error on those layers.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: The cell assignment matches iso_3.15 (KL=0.43614, E514ab09c524e), so the bits are unchanged. This grid uses act_order=true and lowers damp from the default to damp=0.005, so the error compensation relies more on the measured Hessian. The low-bit rht_gptq_int2 layers carry much of the loss, for example 14.down at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp02_bs64
proposals.rationale: This tests the opposite direction on damp, with the same bits as iso_3.15 (KL=0.43614, E514ab09c524e). It uses act_order=true, damp=0.02 and block_size=64. Stronger damping may generalise better from the 8x512 calibration to the validation windows. The gap between predicted and measured KL (0.398 vs 0.436) suggests the calibration fit does not fully carry over to validation.
